# Tobit Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** They arrived at Ecbatana and came to the house of Raguel. Sarah came out to meet them; she greeted them, and they greeted her in return. She brought them inside.

**7:2** Raguel said to his wife Edna, "How remarkably this young man resembles my kinsman Tobit!"

**7:3** Raguel asked them, "Where are you from, brothers?"

They said to him, "We are sons of Naphtali, from among the captives in Nineveh."

**7:4** He said, "Do you know our kinsman Tobit?"

They said, "We know him."

He asked, "How is he? Is he well?"

**7:5** They said, "He is alive and well."

Then Tobias said, "He is my father."

**7:6** Raguel leaped up and kissed him and burst into tears. He blessed him and said, "You are the son of a noble and good father. How terrible that such a righteous and generous man has lost his sight!"

He embraced his kinsman Tobias and wept.

**7:7** His wife Edna wept over him as well, and their daughter Sarah also wept.

**7:8** Raguel slaughtered a ram from the flock and gave them a warm welcome.

When they had washed, bathed, and reclined at table to eat, Tobias said to Raphael, "Brother Azariah, speak to Raguel to give me Sarah my kinswoman."

**7:9** Raguel overheard this and said to the young man, "Eat and drink and enjoy this evening, brother — for there is no one else who has the right to take my daughter Sarah except you, and I am not free to give her to any other man, since you are her nearest kinsman. But let me be honest with you, my son:

**7:10** I have given her to seven men from among our kinsmen, and every one of them died on the night he went in to her. But now, my son, eat and drink, and the Lord will deal graciously with you."

Tobias said, "I will not eat or drink anything here until you settle this matter and make a decision for me."

Raguel said, "Take her then, here and now. By the decree of the book of Moses she is given to you — it is decreed from heaven that she be given to you. Take her, your kinswoman; from now on you are her brother and she is your sister. She is given to you from this day forward and forever. May the Lord of heaven prosper you this night, my son, and grant you his mercy and peace."

**7:11** Raguel called his daughter Sarah, and she came to him. He took her by the hand and gave her to Tobias, saying: "Take her in accordance with the law and the decree written in the book of Moses. Take her and bring her safely to your father. May the God of heaven grant you a prosperous journey in peace."

**7:12** Then he called her mother Edna, and he took a scroll and drew up a marriage contract, and they affixed their seals to it.

**7:13** Then they began to eat.

**7:14** Raguel called his wife Edna and said to her, "My sister, prepare the other bedroom and bring her there."

**7:15** She went and prepared the bed in the room as he had told her, and she led Sarah there and wept over her. She wiped away her tears and said to her,

**7:16** "Take heart, dear daughter — may the Lord of heaven give you joy in place of your grief. Take heart."

And she left.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on preserving the three-fold weeping scene (Raguel, Edna, Sarah at vv. 6–7) as the emotional signature of the hospitality sequence. The legal formula at v. 10 ("you are her brother and she is your sister") was retained by EMET and LOGOS; PNEUMA expanded it, prompting discussion (see Disagreement Log). Edna's final words at v. 16 — "Take heart" repeated twice — were preserved by all translators as a deliberate rhetorical doubling.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA's Resolution |
|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| 7:2 | "How-very-much the-young-man resembles Tobit" | "How remarkably this young man resembles my kinsman Tobit!" | "That young man — he looks just like my cousin Tobit" | LOGOS — complete exclamation; "cousin" (PNEUMA) is less precise than "kinsman" for the Greek *syngenēs* |
| 7:3 | "brothers" | "brothers" | "friends" | EMET/LOGOS — "brothers" is the Greek *adelphoi*, preserved as the conventional address between fellow exiles |
| 7:6 | "How-wretched it-is that a-righteous and merciful man has-become-blind" | "How terrible that such a righteous and generous man has lost his sight!" | "What a tragedy — that a man so righteous and so kind should lose his sight!" | LOGOS — preserves "righteous" and "generous/merciful" while being natural; PNEUMA's "tragedy" is too theatrical |
| 7:8 | "they-received them warmly" | "gave them a warm welcome" | "set out a proper welcome for them" | LOGOS — "gave them a warm welcome" is idiomatic and natural |
| 7:9 | "I myself am-not-free to-give her to-any-other-man" | "I am not free to give her to any other man" | "I'm not legally free to give her to anyone else" | LOGOS — "not free" preserves the legal constraint without PNEUMA's added "legally" |
| 7:10 | "Take [her] right-here and now" | "Take her then, here and now" | "All right — she's yours, right here and now" | LOGOS — direct and complete; PNEUMA's "All right" is too colloquial |
| 7:10 | "you-are her-brother, and she-is your-sister" | "you are her brother and she is your sister" | "you are her husband and she is your wife" (expanded) | LOGOS — the marriage formula "brother/sister" must be preserved as-is; it is an ANE convention, not biological kinship. PNEUMA's expansion loses the formulaic character |
| 7:11 | "according-to the-decree written in-the-book of-Moses" | "in accordance with the law and the decree written in the book of Moses" | "according to the law written in the book of Moses" | LOGOS — both "law" (*nomos*) and "decree" (*krima*) are present in the Greek; PNEUMA drops "decree" |
| 7:12 | "a-marriage-contract" | "a marriage contract" | "the marriage contract" | LOGOS — indefinite article retained; the document is being created here for the first time |
| 7:14 | "Sister, prepare..." | "My dear, prepare..." | "Edna, prepare..." | EMET — "Sister" is the Greek *adelphē*, Raguel's address to his wife. This is the same "brother/sister" marital idiom from v. 10. LOGOS's "my dear" interprets; PNEUMA's first-name address modernizes. "My sister" is the SOPHIA resolution |
| 7:16 | "Take-heart, child" | "Take heart, dear daughter" | "Be brave, my darling" | LOGOS blend — "Take heart, dear daughter" captures both the imperative (*tharsei*) and the term of address (*teknon* = child/daughter). PNEUMA's "Be brave" slightly shifts the meaning |
